answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce, slashable bond: each identity locks tokens before it can vote or claim work, and rewards accrue only after peers verify completed tasks. If an operator splits one agent into a thousand fake identities, those identities still need separate bonds, while colluding to approve worthless work risks forfeiting them. The rule does not make Sybils impossible; it makes extra identities costly. A garden task might require a juniper planting report and a copper sensor reading, each checked before payout.
